notes: Maps OSHB morphology codes (pinned corpus in corpus-pin.json) to the earliest BBH lesson whose material covers that grammatical feature, or marks them unmapped. Populated in Phase 2 PR D per the mapping policy given to the importer-authoring agent (derived from source/bbh/parsing/lesson_gates.json's verified gates — never invented ad hoc).

PATTERN SYNTAX. A token's morph attribute (e.g. "HTd/Ncmsa") has its language prefix (H=Hebrew, A=Aramaic — Genesis is entirely Hebrew) stripped, then is split on '/' into an ordered list of morpheme segments (e.g. ["Td","Ncmsa"]). The importer forms two kinds of test strings per token: WINDOW 1 = a single segment; WINDOW 2 = two adjacent segments joined by '/' (used only for pronominal-suffix host detection). `morphPattern` is an UNANCHORED regex body — the importer tests it as `new RegExp('^(?:' + morphPattern + ')$')` against the relevant window string(s), per the entry's `window` field (1 or 2; default 1). Every window-1 string in a token MUST match some entry (mapped, unmapped, or neutral) — the generic single-letter-POS catch-all entries below (priority 1) guarantee this; window-2 strings are optional/additive and may match nothing.

ENTRY FIELDS beyond the task's baseline {morphPattern,bbhLesson,unmapped,note}: `window` (1|2, default 1) — which window size this pattern is tested against. `priority` (int, default 0) — when multiple entries match the same window string, the importer picks the highest-priority match; ties are resolved by preferring a mapped match over an unmapped one, then the higher bbhLesson, and are logged as a non-fatal warning by validate_bbh_reader_data.mjs (none are expected to occur with this entry set). `neutral` (bool) — matched, not unmapped, contributes no lesson and does not count toward unmappedCount; used for the bare Sp segment, which is only meaningful when combined with its host via a window-2 rule. `lemmaStrongs` (array of Strong's-number strings) — entry only applies if the window's ALIGNED lemma segment (lemma.split('/')[segmentIndex], with any trailing homonym letter like ' a'/' b' stripped) has this Strong's number; used for the numeral and haya(1961)-imperfect overrides. `isProperName` (bool) — token gets isProperName:true in the emitted data and is excluded from unknown-content-lexeme counts. `vocabLinked` (bool) — this entry's real gate is NOT the literal bbhLesson field; instead the importer resolves it per-token from that token's own vocabLesson match (see the D|Ta|Te|Tj|Tm|Tn|To entry below and tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs for the resolution code).

STEM-FLOOR ENCODING. Per the task policy, Nifal/Hitpael verb forms floor at L37 and Piel/Hifil floor at L29 regardless of their conjugation's own base lesson (e.g. Piel imperfect: base L23 imperfect, but max(23,29)=29). Rather than have the importer compute max() at runtime, every verb entry below already encodes the PRE-COMPUTED max(conjugationBaseLesson, stemFloor) as its bbhLesson — each entry's `note` states both the base lesson and the floor for traceability. Pual/Hofal (stem codes P/H) are UNMAPPED at any conjugation (appendix-only) — no floor applies because there is no ceiling to raise, they are simply out of scope.

SEQUENTIAL PERFECT (weqatal, OSHB conjugation letter 'q') is folded into the ordinary perfect entries (conjugation-letter class '[pq]') — the book treats it as the Perfect form gated by number (L16/L19), not as a separate paradigm; do not add a distinct weqatal gate.

PRIORITY TIERS in use: 100 = numeral lemma override (beats every other N/A rule); 90 = היה imperfect lemma override; 50/40/30 = the three suffix host-detection rules (verb-host / plural-noun-host / fallback-any-host), highest-specificity first; 20 = the main per-POS grammar rules; 1 = per-POS-letter safety-net catch-alls (unmapped) that guarantee every window-1 segment resolves to something even if a real Genesis form was missed when this table was authored.
Populated in Phase 2 PR D alongside tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs. Empty in PR A by design.

Bug-history note: every regex here is tested as ^(?:pattern)$ (a FULL-STRING match) by the importer, not a prefix search — bare POS-letter patterns that are meant to match a variable-length code (the numeral override [AN].*, the haya imperfect override Vqi\d[mfc][sp], the Pual/Hofal V[PH].*, and every generic single-letter safety-net catch-all) MUST end in .* or an explicit variable-length class, or they will only ever match the bare 1-2 char POS code itself and silently never fire. Caught via tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs --report's coverage-gap count during PR D authoring; fixed before the first `selections.json` curation pass.

Common/gentilic noun, singular, absolute state — L7 noun endings.
Common/gentilic noun, plural or dual, absolute state — L10 plural/dual endings.
Common/gentilic noun, any number, construct state — L20 bound/construct state (supersedes the abs. sg/pl gates for this token; construct is taught as its own category regardless of number).

Proper noun (name) — names appear in readings from the earliest lessons (L5 independent-pronoun lesson introduces the first narrative material); marked isProperName so it is excluded from unknown-content-lexeme counts.
Noun form not matched by the common/gentilic/proper rules above (e.g. Aramaic 'determined' state, which does not occur in Genesis but is guarded here). Safety-net catch-all.

Adjective (any type/gender/number/state) — L32 adjective inflection. Construct-state adjectives still land here: max(L32 adjective, L20 construct) = L32, so no separate construct rule is needed for adjectives.
Adjective form not matched by the rule above. Safety-net catch-all.

Numerals 1-10 (Strong's 259 אחד, 8147 שניים, 7969 שלוש, 702 ארבע, 2568 חמש, 8337 שש, 7651 שבע, 8083 שמונה, 8672 תשע, 6235 עשר), tagged by OSHB as noun or adjective — overridden to L45 (numerals lesson) regardless of the underlying N/A morph shape. Priority 100 beats every other N/A rule.
Personal (independent) pronoun, singular — L5 singular subject pronouns.
Personal (independent) pronoun, plural — L11 plural subject pronouns.
Demonstrative pronoun (near/far) — L33 demonstratives.
Interrogative pronoun — L14 interrogative-words table is the grammar gate (מי/מה individually enter vocab earlier at L6/L8, tracked separately via vocabLesson).
Pronoun type not covered above (indefinite Pf, relative Pr, or malformed) — not taught as a dedicated paradigm in this course. Safety-net catch-all.
Definite article (as its own particle segment) — L8 article.
Interrogative particle (ה‐ yes/no question marker family) — L14 interrogatives table.

Relative particle אשר — L30 (Main and Subordinate Clauses). Checked against the vocab CSV per the task brief: אשר is NOT present as its own vocab row anywhere in source/bbh/Beginning_Biblical_Hebrew_Vocabulary_by_Lesson.csv, so there is no earlier vocab lesson to defer to — the L30 grammar gate stands as authored.

Adverbs (D) and the closed-class particles affirmation/emphasis (Ta), entreaty 'נא' (Te), interjection (Tj), demonstrative/existential particles e.g. הנה/כן/יש (Tm), negative לא (Tn), and the direct-object marker את/אות (To) have no dedicated syntax paradigm lesson in this course — per the task brief's explicit instruction for adverbs ('gate by vocabulary presence only, grammar gate 1'), extended uniformly to this whole closed-class-particle family for the same reason (each is either core vocabulary taught from an early lesson, e.g. לא/את/כן at L5, יש at L12, or has no in-course paradigm at all). vocabLinked:true tells the importer to resolve this token's grammar contribution from its OWN vocabLesson match: found-in-CSV -> flat L1 (always in scope, effectively ungated); not found -> unmapped. See gate-map.json notes and tools/import_oshb_reader.mjs for the resolution code.
Particle type not covered above. Safety-net catch-all.
Preposition, with or without the fused article (Rd) — L13 (ו/ב/כ/ל/מן attach directly to the following word).
Preposition form not matched by Rd? above. Should not fire in practice; safety-net catch-all.
Conjunction ו — L13 (taught alongside the attaching prepositions).

Directional he (Sd), paragogic nun (Sn), paragogic he (Sh) — task policy: directional/paragogic suffixes are UNMAPPED (appendix-only). Sh grouped in with Sd/Sn as the same paragogic-suffix family though not separately named in the task brief.

Bare pronominal suffix segment, standalone. Never scored on its own — always co-occurs with a preceding host segment, which is what the window:2 host+suffix rules below actually score. neutral:true means: matched, not unmapped, contributes no lesson (prevents the generic 'S' catch-all from wrongly flagging every suffixed word as unmapped).
Suffix type not covered above. Safety-net catch-all.
Pronominal suffix on a verb host (any stem/conjugation) — L40 object pronouns attached to verbs. Highest priority among the three suffix-host rules.
Pronominal suffix on a plural/dual noun host — L31 (attached pronouns, plural-host set, completing L22).

Pronominal suffix on any other host (singular noun, preposition R/Rd, direct-object marker To, etc.) — L22 (attached pronouns, singular-host set). Lowest-priority fallback among the three suffix-host rules — fires only when neither the verb-host nor plural-noun-host rule above matched.
